changes: Scoped selection reserves host upload backing plus device upload/output/readback buffers before device work.
Pre-admit the result mask using the parent stage reservation contract and an independent result scope.
Workspace and mask survive caller-scope disposal until asynchronous device work settles; only the mask transfers to the caller on success.

coverage: Dawn selection produces the correct mask at exact peak; one byte less rejects with LAKEQL_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.
A four-row one-column selection reserves 100 backing bytes at peak and retains only its four-byte result.
Pre-admitted parent stage capacity is consumed without double reservation.
Controlled pending pipeline failure verifies reservations remain live after caller-scope disposal and are released after all four device buffers are destroyed.

remaining: Planner allocation-scope capability remains disabled until descriptor and persistent pipeline-cache accounting are covered.
The new reservation counts explicit backing, not GPU-driver metadata, total JavaScript heap or whole-Worker RSS.
Required scoped WebGPU selection remains a compatibility gap; reduction/vector scoped admission is separate unfinished work.
